The skills we currently have are proficiency in relevant coding languages for the project. We also have digital art & animation experience.
summary: Sol 33 is an interactive p5.js and p5play browser game where players manage a 33-day crewed Mars mission, and balance power, shielding, supplies, and radiation through environmental crises. The project transforms complex space science into an engaging experience by integrating real-time NASA open data. Players select authentic landing sites via NASA Mars Trek, respond to live solar flare alerts from the NASA CCMC DONKI API, and face trade-offs informed by NASA research. By turning technical telemetry into a human-centered survival challenge, Sol 33 makes planetary exploration accessible and fosters global STEM literacy, especially in kids aged 7-12.
details:
What It Does & How It Works: Sol 33 is an interactive, browser-based narrative decision-tree science simulation where players manage a 33-day crewed mission on the Martian surface. Starting from landing site selection, players navigate branching scenarios, daily scientific tasks (like NIR spectrometry scans and solar panel dust maintenance), and sudden environmental hazards. Every decision dynamically updates four real-time telemetry metrics: Power, Radiation Shielding, Food/Water Supplies, and Absorbed Radiation Dose (mSv). This leads to multiple mission endings alongside a personalized decision log and official NASA citations at the end.

Benefits & Intended Impact

- Our game wants to make space education accessible by translating complex planetary telemetry and space science concepts into intuitive, hands-on decision-making for students (particularly aged 7-12) and the general public.

- Our game connects gameplay directly to live space agency data, therefore teaching players the engineering trade-offs astronauts face between scientific discovery and crew safety.

- We aim to inspire future explorers by bridging the gap between space agencies and everyday browser users, thereby building science literacy and excitement around humanity's future outside of Earth, like on Mars.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

- Languages & Libraries: JavaScript, HTML, CSS, p5.js (canvas rendering and UI), and p5play (interactive sprite mechanics).

- NASA Open Data & APIs: NASA CCMC DONKI API (real-time solar flare alerts and space weather notifications), and NASA Mars Trek (orbital maps and coordinates for Gale Crater and Vera Rubin Ridge).

- Development & Deployment: Visual Studio Code, Git/GitHub, and Vercel.

Creativity and Design Factors

- All pixel art used in the game has been originally made to make the theme of our game distinct. We also used expressive astronaut character states throughout the game.

- Rather than using static, pre-written space events, the simulation pulls live solar flare classifications directly from NASA's DONKI telemetry feed.

Factors Considered:

Our team prioritized zero-barrier accessibility (running smoothly in any standard web browser without downloads), scientific authenticity (ensuring every resource trade-off reflects real Martian physics, such as atmospheric dust accumulation on solar arrays, + making sure all information present in the game is accurate according to NASA and partner org sources), and replayability through branching mission outcomes.
